haiku-low.q1: No session. It creates a login_challenges row and sets the mfa cookie, then shows code entry. Nothing else is granted.
haiku-low.q2: Only after a valid code from the pending secret is confirmed. Confirm sets totp_enabled true and moves the pending secret to active.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code is consumed atomically, a normal session starts, and an email is queued after commit. Sign-in does not depend on the email, which retries in the background.
haiku-low.q4: Five wrong entries or five minutes elapsed. The challenge is deleted and the user goes back to /login to start again from the password.
haiku-low.q5: On confirming setup, every other session is signed out. The current session stays. Sessions are removed where token_hash differs from the current sid.
haiku-low.q6: No. A step is accepted only if greater than totp_last_step, via an atomic update. Drift tolerance is the current 30-second step plus or minus one step.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: pending moves to active, pending clears, totp_enabled becomes true, totp_last_step is set, old recovery codes are deleted, 10 new ones inserted, other sessions signed out. Partial-failure behaviour is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Stored in the login_challenges table, keyed by token hash. The browser holds the raw token in the httponly mfa cookie, separate from sid. Removed on success, fifth wrong entry, or expiry at 5 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: Active secret: users.totp_secret_sealed. Pending: users.totp_pending_sealed. Replay state: users.totp_last_step. Recovery codes: hashed rows in recovery_codes. 2FA on means totp_enabled is true.
haiku-low.q10: The old secret and old recovery codes stay active until confirmation, so sign-in is unaffected. Abandoning (cancel) clears the pending column and keeps the old secret.
haiku-low.q11: An entry matching recovery-code format is checked as a recovery code, otherwise as TOTP. Wrong or used recovery codes do count as wrong entries toward the five-attempt limit.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED as a path. The LockedOut state is OPEN, product has not decided, and nothing is designed or built, so the user cannot sign in today.

sonnet.q1: Nothing but a challenge: no session and no sid cookie. login() inserts a login_challenges row (attempts 0, expires in 5 minutes), sets the mfa cookie and shows the code entry page. Every other route still requires sid.
sonnet.q2: When a valid code from the pending secret is submitted (confirm). That moves it into totp_secret_sealed, which sign-in reads, and sets totp_enabled = true. Until then sign-in ignores the pending secret.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is consumed atomically (used_at set, only if unused). The server reads how many unused codes remain and creates a normal 30-day sid session. After commit, enqueue_email(user_id, "recovery_code_used", {remaining: n}) queues a notice. Sign-in does not depend on the email: the queue retries in the background, so a mail failure never delays or fails sign-in.
sonnet.q4: The 5th wrong entry, or 5 minutes elapsing (a missing or expired challenge is rejected when used). The challenge row is deleted and the user is sent back to /login to start again from the password.
sonnet.q5: On confirm, every other session is signed out (DELETE FROM sessions for that user except the current sid). The current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. A step is accepted only if it is greater than totp_last_step, via an atomic UPDATE, so a replayed code is rejected and two concurrent requests with the same code cannot both succeed. Drift tolerance is the current 30-second step plus one step either side (-1, 0, +1).
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: the pending secret moves into totp_secret_sealed and the pending column is cleared; totp_enabled is set to true; totp_last_step is set to the accepted step; all old recovery_codes rows are deleted and 10 new hashes inserted; all other sessions are deleted. A wrong code returns an error and nothing changes (stays pending; for a replacement the old secret and codes stay active). What happens if the transaction itself fails partway is NOT STATED, though the single transaction implies the changes go together.
sonnet.q8: In the login_challenges table (token_hash PK, user_id, expires_at, attempts). The browser holds the raw token in the mfa cookie (httponly, secure, Lax), separate from sid. Only the hash is stored. It is removed by deletion on a valid entry (cookie cleared too), on the 5th wrong entry, or when it is rejected as expired. Expired rows are also purged periodically.
sonnet.q9: Active secret: users.totp_secret_sealed (sealed). Pending secret: users.totp_pending_sealed. Enrolment status: users.totp_enabled, which is the 2FA-on flag and becomes true only on a valid confirm. Replay state: users.totp_last_step. Recovery codes: the recovery_codes table (user_id, code_hash, used_at), one row per code, hashes only. 2FA on is determined by totp_enabled, which is the only part of the lifecycle that sign-in reads.
sonnet.q10: The old secret and old recovery codes stay active until confirmation, and sign-in ignores the pending secret and reads only the active column. A wrong code leaves the old secret active. Starting a replacement requires re-entering the password. If the user cancels, the pending column is cleared and the account returns to On with the old secret kept.
sonnet.q11: By format: an entry that matches the format of a recovery code is checked as a recovery code, and anything else is checked as a TOTP code. Yes, a wrong, unknown or already-used recovery code counts as a wrong entry, with the same atomic attempts increment toward the limit of 5.
sonnet.q12: There is none. This is the OPEN LockedOut state. Product has not decided whether support can reset 2FA or how identity would be verified. No reset flow, support tool or contact-support copy is specified. Today that user cannot sign in.
